items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Function names are clear (renderSkuTableAndLogs, openDangerConfirmModal), but handlers use many cryptic abbreviations: `fb`, `fn`, `ord`, `oid`, `rid`, `inp`, `res`, `a`. Business logic has few comments in a 3689-line file.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The single 3689-line index.html (cap: accept). setupEventListeners() runs from about line 3260 to 3680 (~420 lines): one huge function of if-chains for every UI action. That is far over 100 lines, so it is capped at bad.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: API returns {ok:false,error}, and import failure is shown as 'original data protected'. Gaps: Number('') counts as 0 in aftersale qty, and the FileReader has no onerror. Magic values such as the 600ms timeout and the 10% member discount appear inline.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Cancel and reset go through openDangerConfirmModal with clear messages, and statuses gate the allowed actions. But confirm-return ('confirm-return' handler) runs immediately with no confirmation, and btn-execute-import overwrites data without asking first.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: UI handlers call the same apiPay/apiShip/apiCancel/apiConfirmReturn/apiImportData used by shopTestAPI. Import is validated before replacing state, and all 25 hidden tests passed. The integer-cent arithmetic and stats derivation are in the omitted part of the diff, so I could not confirm them.
